questions.question: What is a saturated solution, and how can you tell that a solution is saturated?
questions.expected_answer: A saturated solution is one in which no more solute can dissolve at that temperature. You can tell because any extra solute you add stays as solid grains at the bottom, however much you stir. Adding more solvent lets more solute dissolve.

questions.question: How does the temperature of water affect how much sugar dissolves? What can happen when a hot saturated solution cools?
questions.expected_answer: For most solids, hot water can dissolve more solute than cold water, because its particles move faster and are further apart. When a hot saturated solution cools, the water cannot hold as much, so some solute may come out of the solution as crystals.

questions.question: What does insoluble mean? Give three examples and say how insoluble substances can be separated from water.
questions.expected_answer: An insoluble substance does not dissolve in a solvent. Sand, chalk, flour, oil, stones, plastic and wax are insoluble in water. They settle to the bottom or float on top, so they can be separated by settling and decanting, or by filtering.
